result.keyword: What's the best password manager for a small team?
result.markdown:
For a small team, my top recommendation is **1Password**\.

It offers a particularly good balance of security, ease of use, shared password vaults and administrator controls without being overly complicated.

For a team of roughly 3–20 people, I'd shortlist three products: 1Password, Bitwarden and Dashlane.

## Best options compared

![Wachtwoordmanager 1Password | KPN](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/SR9cQiLQIFEFCALVJ5nUtWe25Q29qJVc5LjX65WdCnj5yzmD0dY1kGYKRcHN2028gLjEDLJ1Kkz4elZpmKF_3nFRDEJ56EPcrV1LwREU1riSDOE2qPsulZBrm1uLMFbZk3uGppXxaiJ5LZXh3ClEqc5wBJ1jJuMVahqzv5wwpeyD20eaUwi0i3WuDMRbtYuK?purpose=fullsize)

**1\. 1Password**

(Best overall experience)

- Excellent shared vaults and permissions.
- Easy for non-technical employees.
- Strong admin controls and security reporting.
- Business Starter Pack: \$24.95/month for up to 10 users.
  
  Best if simplicity and employee adoption matter most.
  
  [1Password business plans](https://1password.com/business)

---

![Free High-Quality Bitwarden Logo for Creative Design](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/p0IJzf2NCUQ2t02rqtPWDpe7Tx4YGCRNleASv1NjpztaDI--7OD-0zWJhdBi_4Wn4-v0Hr3hoS6JA2KXHdCOlvvdfHelZm6tTBmFuxgAbBftLkdqobRCpEkp4ysyI4Rm6vafJPMfHi8ri9Tdeng_QKXRw7C7a5ESA6hn8XLhRMLnvM7oFmwZESsO4_SFLJaX?purpose=fullsize)

**2\. Bitwarden**

(Best value)

- Open-source foundations.
- Shared collections and team management.
- Audit logs and directory integration.
- Teams: around \$4/user/month, annually billed.
  
  Best if you want strong functionality without spending too much.
  
  [Bitwarden business plans](https://bitwarden.com/business/)

---

![Keeper Security Logo PNG,  Vector (AI, EPS, CDR, PDF, SVG) - iconLogoVector](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/hjZLLtGaZjkKvsDiCoIrNA749yx3vMYIFoRmmV0blB-pAj7O30nu3RJOVVhVRwgAOkJUfJ3datZ7pfH1wp7yeplrEL3FQ-HNOpCzlVOW0OcMr1CFjIFAx50apRkdH6sYOH31WcP6gfXOxeAN8qubYhHhGYA5yXp1bc7wqtCxjN2WEQuyMALTG1Pwne14BXyG?purpose=fullsize)

**3\. Keeper**

- Strong administrative controls.
- Shared team folders.
- Good access management and auditing.
- Business Starter pricing reported from around \$2/user/month.
  
  Best if access control and administration are priorities.
  
  [Keeper business plans](https://www.keepersecurity.com/business.html)

Prices are indicative USD prices from November 2026, generally with annual billing. Check UK pricing, VAT and plan limits before purchasing. [toolsandthrive.com](https://toolsandthrive.com/best-password-manager-for-small-business/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[geekchamp.com](https://geekchamp.com/best-password-managers-for-small-business-teams-with-shared-access-controls/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[www.softwarecompare.net](https://www.softwarecompare.net/comparison/best-password-manager-for-business?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

## What I'd look for in a small-team password manager

Regardless of which you choose, make sure it supports\:

- **Shared vaults\:** Share company credentials without sending passwords through Slack or email.
- **Individual accounts\:** Everyone has their own login.
- **Two-factor authentication\:** Ideally mandatory for all employees.
- **Granular permissions\:** Staff only access the credentials they need.
- **Offboarding\:** Easily revoke access when someone leaves.
- **Audit logs\:** See important account and administrative activity.

## My recommendation

I'd narrow it down to 1Password and Bitwarden.

- Choose 1Password if you want the smoothest experience.
- Choose Bitwarden if you want excellent value and more open-source transparency.

search_results.description: TechRadar’s 2025 guide reviews the best business password managers, emphasizing stronger security, privacy, credential sharing, employee productivity, and compliance. NordPass is recommended as the best overall choice because it combines affordability, ease of use, biometric and multifactor authentication, password sharing, and zero-knowledge XChaCha20 encryption; however, SSO and directory provisioning require its Enterprise plan. Dashlane is praised for general business use and polished administration, while RoboForm stands out for administrators through role-based permissions, provisioning, SSO, and policy controls. Keeper offers strong scalability, auditing, and support, though several integrations and monitoring tools cost extra. ManageEngine Password Manager Pro is a powerful self-hosted option for large enterprises, whereas Bitwarden appeals to organizations seeking open-source transparency. LogMeOnce suits SMBs, Proton Pass prioritizes privacy and data control, 1Password provides granular vault and guest access, and Sticky Password is an affordable choice for small teams. Buyers should assess company size, encryption, MFA, SSO, integrations, support, pricing, and compliance needs. Password managers also identify weak or reused credentials, reduce phishing risk, and improve productivity through autofill and passkeys.
